outline:
學生需於第三學年第二學期開始修習「英文實務專題」，於第四學年第一學期期末正式發表成果。本課程旨在發展學生獨立規劃及從事研究的能力，學生可在指導老師的指導下，依個別的需求選擇研究的方向，訂定題目，並獨立完成研究計畫，撰寫報告。 專題研究範圍含： 實驗研究 量調查研究或質調查研究 個案研究 回溯研究 文化比較研究 理論闡述研究
This course is designed to develop the student's background for planning and conducting research independently. The nature of the project conducted will vary from student to student, but regardless of the genre of the project, it must result in a written research report. The research project must be conducted by the student individually. It is anticipated that the project will result from: an experiment; a descriptive study using quantitative procedures or qualitative procedures; a case study; a historical study; a cross-cultural study; a theory that offers an alternative interpretation to a current theory or model.

By the end of the semester, students will be able to:

- Identify and analyze a specific object or text.
- Formulate a focused research question appropriate for an undergraduate senior project.
- Find existing scholarship related to their research question, summarize relevant sources, place their project in conversation with these texts, and correctly cite, introduce, and explain sources in their writing.
- Define and use key concepts and theoretical terms clearly when discussing their object of analysis.
- Apply at least one theoretical concept or framework to their object of analysis and demonstrate how that theory helps interpret their object source.
- Develop an argument that moves from observation to claim, supported with specific evidence.
- Deliver structured peer feedback on classmates’ projects, identifying strengths, questions, and areas for improvement.
- Revise their own writing in response to feedback from peers and the advisor in order to strengthen clarity, argumentation, and organization.
- Produce a structured draft of a senior project paper that demonstrates sustained analysis and preparation for the final draft and project presentations.
schedule:
Weeks 1–4: Initial Project Meetings
Students meet with the advisor to:
Discuss their current proposals
Identify a manageable object or case study
Begin forming a research question
Deliverable: Project Proposal
Weeks 4–8: Narrowing the Project
Students will:
Narrow the research question
Close read / make observations / note patterns
Identify relevant sources
Define key terms
Deliverable: Observation Notes
Students submit structured notes describing what they observe in their chosen object.
Weeks 8–12: From Observations to Claims
Students begin turning observations into analytical claims.
Focus:
linking observations to interpretations
connecting interpretations to larger arguments
drafting sections of the paper
Advisor meetings will help students:
test whether claims are supported by evidence
refine the project structure
Deliverable: Working Thesis and Outline
Weeks 12–16: Draft Development
Students write major sections of the project.
Focus:
writing analytical paragraphs
integrating sources
strengthening the argument structure
Deliverable: Formal Draft
Weeks 16–18: Revision Toward Full Draft
Students revise their work with advisor feedback.
Focus:
clarifying argument structure
improving evidence and examples
preparing a near-complete draft
Deliverable: Revised Formal Draft
assessment:
1. Project Development Process (60%)
This component evaluates the research process across the semester, including the following milestones:
Project Proposal (Weeks 1–4)
Observation Notes (Weeks 4–8)
Working Thesis and Outline (Weeks 8–12)
Participation in advising meetings
Structured peer feedback on classmates’ projects
Students are assessed on their ability to:
identify a clear object or text for analysis
develop a focused research question
gather observations and identify patterns
define key terms and concepts
locate and summarize relevant scholarship
place their project in conversation with existing sources
provide constructive feedback to peers
2. Formal Draft (20%)
Students submit a substantial draft of their senior project during Weeks 12–16.
The draft should demonstrate:
a clear research question
a developing argument supported by observations and examples
engagement with relevant scholarly sources
explanation and application of at least one theoretical concept
an organized structure with analytical paragraphs
3. Revised Formal Draft (20%)
During Weeks 16–18, students revise their work based on feedback from:
the advisor
peers
their own reflection on the argument and structure.

The revised draft should demonstrate improvement in:
clarity of research question and thesis
strength of claims
integration and explanation of sources
organization and structure
precision of evidence and examples
Evaluation Criteria
Across all components, projects will be assessed based on:
Research Focus
clear research question
appropriate scope
well-defined object of analysis

Use of Sources
relevant scholarship identified
sources introduced and explained clearly
correct citation practices

Conceptual Clarity
key terms and theoretical ideas defined clearly
theory applied meaningfully to the object of analysis

Analytical Development
observations lead to interpretations
interpretations develop into supported claims
argument is supported by specific evidence

Revision and Engagement
responsiveness to feedback
participation in advising meetings
meaningful improvement between drafts
